newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 1996/97 sugar stocks/use ratio 15.4 pct-US.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 1996/97 sugar stocks/use ratio 15.4 pct-US.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department forecast Monday a 1996/97 sugar stocks-to-use ratio of 15.4 percent, a key figure in setting the import quota.

At the start of fiscal 1997, USDA allocated 1.7 million tonnes of sugar imports and said adjustments would be considered in January, March and May. If the ratio was 15.5 percent of less on the review dates, the quota automatically goes up by 200,000 tonnes. If it is higher, the tranche is canceled.
Increases were denied in January but approved in March.
When an increase is approved, the U.S. trade representative must allocate the additional quota within three business days.
